chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Nat Cole as arranger and the early lean years
summary: They recall Nat's big band, shared ham hocks and beans, and his trio with Wesley Prince and Oscar Moore.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Oh, what was I talking about? I just said that he astounded everybody except Art Tatum. But of course, so many people forgot or never did know what a great musician and pianist Nat Cole was. He also was a great arranger. That's something that people didn't know.
He had a big band here for a while, didn't he? Or he arrived here with a big band?
He came here with...I can't think of the guy's name...a band out of Chicago that's still going... I'll remember that for next time.
I remember John Simmons told me about Nat having a big band down at the Lincoln Theater on Central Avenue.
Right, right. Oh, I can't think of the guy's name who was the bandleader. But Nat, he worked with a show, too... I guess some of it escapes me at the moment.
Well, it will come back before we're through, I'm sure.
It will come back, yeah. Nat and I and Nat's first wife, Nadine, and all of us... Things were

pretty rough during some of that period. I remember we used to go by and share pots of ham hocks and beans, and they were so good... [LAUGHS] And then Nat formed a trio with Wesley Prince, who I understand just passed away recently, and Oscar Moore, who was... Oscar has quit playing, too. I don't know why. He was such a beautiful player.
But anyhow, I don't know how we got off into that.
